                            <img class="eche-report-question-icon" src="https://erasmus-plus.ec.europa.eu/profiles/custom/eac_profile/modules/eac_eche/images/eche-pdf/number-corner-orange-11.png" width="100%" height="100%" alt="Question Icon" title="Question Icon" loading="lazy">

                            <div class="eche-report-officer-number-text">11</div>
                        </div>
                        <div class="eche-officer-question-icon"><img class="eche-report-question-icon" src="https://erasmus-plus.ec.europa.eu/profiles/custom/eac_profile/modules/eac_eche/images/ECHE__OFFICERS_Q11.png" width="100%" height="100%" alt="Question Icon" title="Question Icon" loading="lazy">
</div>
                    </div>
                    <div class="eche-report-title-question-text-wrapper">
                        <div class="eche-officer-question"> At the end of the mobility, your institution has formal procedures for recognising student mobility (good practices linked to recognition at the end of the mobility, e.g. in the use of Transcripts of Records and Grade Distribution Tables)</div>
                        <div class="eche-report-button-js eche-report-detail-close"><i class="fa fa-plus-circle fa-3x"></i></div>
                    </div>
                </div>
                <div class="eche-officer-question-wrapper eche-report-question-wrapper-show">
                    <div class="eche-report-border"></div>
                    <div classs="eche-officer-must">
                                                <h3>Must have</h3>
                                                <span class="eche-officer-user-answer">Transcripts of Records are issued in a timely manner (normally 5 weeks) to both incoming and outgoing students</span>
                        <h4>Guidance note:</h4>
                         <p>It is highly important in the recognition framework to provide Transcripts of Records in a timely manner, immediately following the mobility period. After the mobility, the receiving institution should send a Transcript of Records to the student and to the sending institution within a period stipulated in the Inter-Institutional Agreement (normally within five weeks after publication/proclamation of the student’s results at the receiving institution). It can be provided electronically or through any other means accessible to the student and the sending institution. The Transcript of Records from the receiving institution should refer to the educational components agreed upon in the Learning Agreement. Grade distribution information should be included as well, either as a web link or an annex.</p><p>Following the receipt of the Transcript of Records from the receiving institution, the sending institution should automatically transfer and recognise the student’s academic outcomes successfully completed at the receiving institution, as agreed in the Learning Agreement, without the need for the student to take any further courses or exams. The Sending Institution will provide a Transcript of Records to the student or record the results in a database or any other means accessible to the student, normally within five weeks after having received the transcript of the receiving institution. The EU official template for the Learning Agreement for studies (including the Transcript of Records) is available online: <a href="http://ec.europa.eu/education/opportunities/higher-education/quality-framework_en.htm">http://ec.europa.eu/education/opportunities/higher-education/quality-framework_en.htm</a></p>                         <span class="eche-officer-user-answer">All credits gained by students during a period of study abroad that were specified in the final version of the Learning Agreement are automatically transferred by your institution and count towards the students' final degree, without the need for the student to take any further courses or exams</span>
                        <h4>Guidance note:</h4>
                         <p>The sending institution should ensure that all the credits earned by the mobile student during the mobility period are recognised and counted towards the final degree, without the need for the student to take any further courses or exams. The period of study abroad must be clear in the student's records and documents issued to the student (Diploma Supplement or equivalent). This is a golden rule of recognition of credit mobility within the framework of inter-institutional agreements. All the credits towards the student's degree that are earned during the mobility period and which were originally agreed on in the Learning Agreement (or a revised version to it) should be recognised by the sending HEI without the need for the student to take any further courses or exams. Learning Agreements are binding for all the parties and require that, on successful completion of the mobility period, the sending HEI recognises credits earned by the student and documents these credits in the student records, so they can be identified in a transparent way.</p><p>Upon receipt of the Transcript of Records or Training Certificates, the sending HEI should:<br>a) certify the mobile student has fulfilled all requirements stipulated in the Learning Agreement;<br>b) ensure recognition of the mobility period abroad within the time-scale and according to the conditions stipulated in the institutional recognition framework.</p>                      </div>
                    <div class="eche-officer-best">
                                                <h3>Best practices</h3>
                                                <span class="eche-officer-user-answer">Transcripts of Records of incoming students include a description of or a link to the national grading system</span>
                        <h4>Guidance note:</h4>
                         <p>The Transcript of Records from the receiving institution should include grade distribution information, either as a web link or an annex. The local grading scale should be clearly explained, with a statistical distribution of local grades, to provide transparency and understanding of grading practices at the host institution. Where applicable, use should be made of a Grade Distribution Table for the programme of study, according to the ECTS Users’ Guide (<a href="http://ec.europa.eu/education/ects/users-guide/index.htm">http://ec.europa.eu/education/ects/users-guide/index.htm</a>).</p>                         <span class="eche-officer-user-answer">Grades of outgoing students are converted, if applicable, according to a fair and transparent methodology communicated before the mobility</span>
                        <h4>Guidance note:</h4>
                         <p>Grades of outgoing students are converted, if applicable, according to a fair and transparent methodology communicated before the mobility. There are more details on this in the ECTS Users’ Guide.</p>                         <span class="eche-officer-user-answer">In addition to recognising formal learning, the institution recognises any non-formal or informal learning acquired during the mobility according to the ECTS Users’ Guide, e.g. by awarding ECTS credits for volunteering</span>
                        <h4>Guidance note:</h4>
                         <p>During a period of mobility, students often take advantage of other opportunities outside of their required courses. These may include specific activities which can be considered non-formal or informal learning where they have acquired new skills. This could include additional language and cultural courses, extra-curricular activities, setting up a business and volunteer work undertaken by the student in that period or upon return at the receiving institution.</p>                      </div>
                    <div class="eche-officer-case">
                                                <h3>Case studies</h3>
                                                <div><a href="https://erasmus-plus.ec.europa.eu/eche/standing-out-from-the-crowd-supporting-students-through-full-recognition-and-documenting-of-mobility-outcomes" target="_blank">"Standing out from the crowd" - supporting students through full recognition and documenting of mobility outcomes</a></div>
                                                <div><a href="https://erasmus-plus.ec.europa.eu/eche/a-common-approach-to-ects-grade-conversion-ensuring-a-fair-assessment-of-student-performance-after-study-abroad" target="_blank">A common approach to ECTS grade conversion, ensuring a fair assessment of student performance after study abroad</a></div>
                                             </div>
                    <div class="eche-report-button-js eche-report-detail-close-text"><i class="fa fa-times fa-2x"></i><span>Close</span></div>
                </div>
            </div>
                         <div class="eche-report-full-question-wrapper">
                <div class="eche-officer-question-title-wrapper">
                    <div class="eche-report-title-icons-wrapper">
                                                 <div class="eche-report-officer-number">
                            <img class="eche-report-question-icon" src="https://erasmus-plus.ec.europa.eu/profiles/custom/eac_profile/modules/eac_eche/images/eche-pdf/number-corner-orange-12.png" width="100%" height="100%" alt="Question Icon" title="Question Icon" loading="lazy">

                            <div class="eche-report-officer-number-text">12</div>
                        </div>
                        <div class="eche-officer-question-icon"><img class="eche-report-question-icon" src="https://erasmus-plus.ec.europa.eu/profiles/custom/eac_profile/modules/eac_eche/images/ECHE__OFFICERS_Q12.png" width="100%" height="100%" alt="Question Icon" title="Question Icon" loading="lazy">
</div>
                    </div>
                    <div class="eche-report-title-question-text-wrapper">
                        <div class="eche-officer-question"> Your institution issues a Diploma Supplement</div>
                        <div class="eche-report-button-js eche-report-detail-close"><i class="fa fa-plus-circle fa-3x"></i></div>
                    </div>
                </div>
                <div class="eche-officer-question-wrapper eche-report-question-wrapper-show">
                    <div class="eche-report-border"></div>
                    <div classs="eche-officer-must">
                                                <h3>Must have</h3>
                                                <span class="eche-officer-user-answer">To all students, automatically, free of charge and in a major European language</span>
                        <h4>Guidance note:</h4>
                         <p>This Supplement should include a record of the period of mobility under the Erasmus+ Programme. The 48 European countries taking part in the Bologna Process have agreed that each mobile graduate in their respective country should receive the Diploma Supplement (DS) automatically, free of charge and in at least one of the major European languages in addition to the national language. The HEI should issue a Diploma Supplement (or equivalent) to accompany every degree successfully completed by a student, using - where applicable - the template developed by the European Commission, the Council of Europe and UNESCO. The HEI's policy on issuing the Diploma Supplement should be published on its website.</p><p>The template for the Diploma Supplement is available at:<br><a href="http://ec.europa.eu/education/tools/diploma-supplement_en.htm">http://ec.europa.eu/education/tools/diploma-supplement_en.htm&nbsp;</a></p>                      </div>
                    <div class="eche-officer-best">
                                                <h3>Best practices</h3>
                                                <span class="eche-officer-user-answer">That includes a record of the mobility period(s) carried out by the student under the Erasmus+ programme</span>
                        <h4>Guidance note:</h4>
                         <p>The information contained in the Transcript of Records from the Receiving Institution should also be included in the Diploma Supplement produced by the Sending Institution (at least for Sending Institutions located in Programme Countries), with the exact titles of the components that the student has followed abroad. Alongside modules or units taken at the sending HEI, the Diploma Supplement should list recognised modules, units and/or training activities undertaken during the student's mobility period and indicate the location of these mobility activities.<br>In the case of double, multiple or joint degrees, the Diploma Supplement should indicate the name and status of the partner HEIs awarding the degree and explain the respective language(s) of instruction and examination. In addition, an explanation should be provided about the grading and classification scheme agreed by the awarding HEIs. The template for the Diploma Supplement is available at:<br><a href="http://ec.europa.eu/education/tools/diploma-supplement_en.htm">http://ec.europa.eu/education/tools/diploma-supplement_en.htm</a>&nbsp;</p>                      </div>
                    <div class="eche-officer-case">
                                                <h3>Case studies</h3>
                                                <div><a href="https://erasmus-plus.ec.europa.eu/eche/the-diploma-supplement-a-tool-to-promote-international-recognition-and-transparency-of-academic-achievement" target="_blank">The Diploma Supplement – a tool to promote international recognition and transparency of academic achievement</a></div>
                                             </div>
                    <div class="eche-report-button-js eche-report-detail-close-text"><i class="fa fa-times fa-2x"></i><span>Close</span></div>
                </div>
            </div>
                         <div class="eche-report-full-question-wrapper">
                <div class="eche-officer-question-title-wrapper">
                    <div class="eche-report-title-icons-wrapper">
                                                 <div class="eche-report-officer-number">
                            <img class="eche-report-question-icon" src="https://erasmus-plus.ec.europa.eu/profiles/custom/eac_profile/modules/eac_eche/images/eche-pdf/number-corner-orange-13.png" width="100%" height="100%" alt="Question Icon" title="Question Icon" loading="lazy">

                            <div class="eche-report-officer-number-text">13</div>
                        </div>
                        <div class="eche-officer-question-icon"><img class="eche-report-question-icon" src="https://erasmus-plus.ec.europa.eu/profiles/custom/eac_profile/modules/eac_eche/images/ECHE__OFFICERS_Q13.png" width="100%" height="100%" alt="Question Icon" title="Question Icon" loading="lazy">
</div>
                    </div>
                    <div class="eche-report-title-question-text-wrapper">
                        <div class="eche-officer-question"> Your institution promotes and recognises staff mobility</div>
                        <div class="eche-report-button-js eche-report-detail-close"><i class="fa fa-plus-circle fa-3x"></i></div>
                    </div>
                </div>
                <div class="eche-officer-question-wrapper eche-report-question-wrapper-show">
                    <div class="eche-report-border"></div>
                    <div classs="eche-officer-must">
                                                <h3>Must have</h3>
                                                <span class="eche-officer-user-answer">By taking it into account in the assessment of their professional development </span>
                        <h4>Guidance note:</h4>
                         <p>Participation in international projects should be seen as an important aspect of the professional development of the staff and of the modernisation of the HEI and should, therefore, be considered a key component in staff evaluation practices.</p><p>The HEI should link its HR strategy to the objectives set out the internationalisation strategy for staff. For all staff who undertake a period of mobility, HR should be informed and provide support to ensure the identification of the professional development needs of the individual as well as setting out agreed career objectives for their period of mobility. This can be through prepared addendums to staff contracts or through less formal mechanisms of agreed objectives. The new objectives should become part of the normal system of staff evaluation or appraisal and be used in order to recognise the achievements of the staff during the period of mobility. This means that HR staff should be trained to ensure these additional objectives are formally evidenced and recorded in staff records and lead to other rewards and recognition.&nbsp;</p>                         <span class="eche-officer-user-answer">Through, for example the reduction of the teaching load, promotion or pay rises</span>
                        <h4>Guidance note:</h4>
                         <p>It is highly important to incentivise staff to participate in mobility activities. In order to support and encourage mobility, HEIs should provide a number of incentives to ensure that when staff return to the sending institution, they have long term career benefits. HEIs should acknowledge periods of mobility as a normal part of a career path. Staff working schedules and agreed objectives (in terms of research outputs and assessments) should be adapted to meet their new requirements. Temporary replacements should be found during the mobility period, where possible, to ensure continuity during the mobility period. Upon returning to the sending institution, incentives to maintain links with other institutions or networks should be put in place through providing the time to nurture new relationships (reduction in teaching or research loads, continued related objectives set in performance appraisals). The new objectives set with HR for the period of mobility should be ones which are explicitly recognised and rewarded through promotion, awards or pay rises. Additional cultural / language skills should be recognised as a component in any evaluation / assessment of the staff. This may be achieved by making it well-known that participation is a formal part of staff evaluation procedures, and may lead to improvements in both working conditions and promotion or broader career prospects.</p>                      </div>
                    <div class="eche-officer-best">
                                                <h3>Best practices</h3>
                                                <span class="eche-officer-user-answer">By encouraging them to propose improvements to the institutional strategy for internationalisation and overarching structure, as well as for structural reform</span>
                        <h4>Guidance note:</h4>
                         <p>One important form of recognition for staff, which is equally beneficial to the HEI is to encourage their involvement in improving internationalisation and structural reform within the institution. This includes the opportunity for staff to provide feedback into the management structures of departments and the overall institution. There should be a firm commitment - perhaps in writing - from the HEI to recognise and make use of constructive feedback as well as the appropriate forums for staff to engage with senior management to discuss their experiences and propose new ideas for improvement.&nbsp;</p>                         <span class="eche-officer-user-answer">By inviting them to share new learning and teaching practices developed abroad with their peers in the institution</span>
                        <h4>Guidance note:</h4>
                         <p>The experience of staff should be valued and shared as an inspiration to others, by, for example, organising meetings and publishing articles where the mobile participants share their experience and the impact of mobility on their personal and professional development. Where staff are involved in teaching at host institutions, new learning and teaching practices can be brought back and shared with other staff members through seminars or presentations. Staff can be supported through the administrative and academic services to understand the skills they have acquired and how best to use them within their own institution.</p>                         <span class="eche-officer-user-answer">By encouraging them to propose cooperation projects with their receiving organisation</span>
                        <h4>Guidance note:</h4>
                         <p>Mobile staff bring back new partners, networks and ideas which can be of significant value for the HEI. Staff should be encouraged to propose and develop new or further cooperation projects between their receiving and sending institutions. This requires time and commitment, which need to be given formally by the sending institution, including, for example, additional support to write joint proposals.&nbsp;</p>                      </div>
                    <div class="eche-officer-case">
                                                <h3>Case studies</h3>
                                                <div><a href="https://erasmus-plus.ec.europa.eu/eche/recognition-of-staff-mobility-supporting-individuals-development-and-institutional-aims-and-objectives" target="_blank">Recognition of staff mobility – supporting individuals’ development and institutional aims and objectives</a></div>
                                                <div><a href="https://erasmus-plus.ec.europa.eu/eche/recognition-of-staff-participating-in-erasmus-staff-mobility-actions-and-international-cooperation-projects" target="_blank">Recognition of staff participating in Erasmus staff mobility actions and international cooperation projects</a></div>
                                             </div>
                    <div class="eche-report-button-js eche-report-detail-close-text"><i class="fa fa-times fa-2x"></i><span>Close</span></div>
                </div>
            </div>
                         <div class="eche-report-full-question-wrapper">
                <div class="eche-officer-question-title-wrapper">
                    <div class="eche-report-title-icons-wrapper">
                                                 <div class="eche-report-officer-number">
                            <img class="eche-report-question-icon" src="https://erasmus-plus.ec.europa.eu/profiles/custom/eac_profile/modules/eac_eche/images/eche-pdf/number-corner-orange-14.png" width="100%" height="100%" alt="Question Icon" title="Question Icon" loading="lazy">

                            <div class="eche-report-officer-number-text">14</div>
                        </div>
                        <div class="eche-officer-question-icon"><img class="eche-report-question-icon" src="https://erasmus-plus.ec.europa.eu/profiles/custom/eac_profile/modules/eac_eche/images/ECHE__OFFICERS_Q14.png" width="100%" height="100%" alt="Question Icon" title="Question Icon" loading="lazy">
</div>
                    </div>
                    <div class="eche-report-title-question-text-wrapper">
                        <div class="eche-officer-question"> With regards to the outcomes and experiences of Erasmus+ activities</div>
                        <div class="eche-report-button-js eche-report-detail-close"><i class="fa fa-plus-circle fa-3x"></i></div>
                    </div>
                </div>
                <div class="eche-officer-question-wrapper eche-report-question-wrapper-show">
                    <div class="eche-report-border"></div>
                    <div classs="eche-officer-must">
                                                <h3>Must have</h3>
                                                <span class="eche-officer-user-answer">The results are monitored, evaluated and disseminated as a way to improve international cooperation and mobility activities</span>
                        <h4>Guidance note:</h4>
                         <p>Linked with the overall internationalisation strategy of the institution, monitoring and evaluation of cooperation projects and Erasmus+ mobility is essential if HEIs are to learn from their experiences. Monitoring and evaluation is more than just measuring the number and types of outputs, it needs to include capturing information on the overall outcomes and experiences of the activities at the institutional and the individual level. Systematic monitoring and evaluation should therefore include more qualitative approaches, which expressly capture the experiences in a way which helps the institution to understand the added value of its involvement in these activities. Documenting and analysing the outcomes and experiences is only the first step. To learn from the approaches taken, and the benefits gained, institutions should take time to disseminate the findings of the cooperation projects and mobility periods through, for example, meetings, workshops and publications, social media, etc. These activities will embed good practice, help the institution to iteratively improve its approach and also feed back into the on-going monitoring and evaluation.</p>                         <span class="eche-officer-user-answer">The results are used systematically for the benefit of your institution, providing internationalisation at home, hence enhancing intercultural competences of non-mobile students and staff</span>
                        <h4>Guidance note:</h4>
                         <p>The outcomes and experiences of cooperation and Erasmus+ mobility have a much wider impact than just improving mobile activities. All institutions have significant numbers of non-mobile staff and students who can benefit from the international experiences of others. As part of the monitoring and evaluation processes, HEIs should consider the impact which can be specifically made on non-mobile staff and students, giving them “internationalisation at home experiences”. This includes building international competences, cultural awareness, virtual mobility opportunities, inviting international lecturers and embedding student projects with an international focus into the curricula, and providing opportunities for local students to work together with incoming mobile participants in e.g. project work, to ensure that local students benefit from the presence of mobile students at their institution. This fits with the activities of disseminating the overall outcomes and experiences of the cooperation projects and Erasmus+ mobility, though tailored to a different audience. It should take into account the professional development needs of the staff at the HEI and the perspectives of non-mobile students.&nbsp;</p>                      </div>
                    <div class="eche-officer-best">
                                                <h3>Best practices</h3>
                                                <span class="eche-officer-user-answer">The results are exploited and disseminated, by providing participants with the results of cooperation projects and Erasmus+ mobility opportunities (e.g. presentations) to share funding possibilities</span>
                        <h4>Guidance note:</h4>
                         <p>The dissemination of outcomes is an integral part of mobility projects. Good practice would be to ensure that the dissemination is built into the support measure and participants in projects and mobility actions are allocated adequate time, resources and space to disseminate their experiences and exploit project results. This includes opportunities to share new knowledge and to highlight new opportunities (including funding) which have arisen from the new relationships formed. In order to do this, HEIs should provide support functions such as web platforms to collect results or opportunities to present results at the institutional or departmental level, as relevant.&nbsp;</p>                         <span class="eche-officer-user-answer">After the mobility Erasmus+ participants have the opportunity to present their newly acquired competences</span>
                        <h4>Guidance note:</h4>
                         <p>The study entitled ‘Effects of mobility on the skills and employability of students and the internationalisation of higher education institutions’ showcases how mobility can contribute to the internationalisation of higher education institutions, including the impacts on teaching methods, cooperation between HEIs and perception of staff more generally. Therefore the dissemination of outcomes is an integral part of mobility projects. Good practice would be to ensure that the dissemination is built into the support measure and participants in projects and mobility actions are allocated adequate time, resources and space to disseminate their experiences and exploit project results. This includes opportunities to share new knowledge and to highlight new opportunities (including funding) which have arisen from the new relationships formed. In order to do this, HEIs should provide support functions such as web platforms to collect results or opportunities to present results at the institutional or departmental level, as relevant.&nbsp;</p>                      </div>
                    <div class="eche-officer-case">
                                                <h3>Case studies</h3>
                                                <div><a href="https://erasmus-plus.ec.europa.eu/eche/capitalising-on-the-outcomes-and-experiences-of-erasmus-activities" target="_blank">Capitalising on the outcomes and experiences of Erasmus+ activities</a></div>
                                                <div><a href="https://erasmus-plus.ec.europa.eu/eche/the-erasmus-impact-study-effects-of-mobility-on-the-skills-and-employability-of-students-and-the-internationalisation-of-higher-education-institutions" target="_blank">The Erasmus Impact Study: Effects of mobility on the skills and employability of students and the internationalisation of higher education institutions</a></div>
                                             </div>

                </div>

{"data":[{"slug":"software-developer-net-c-all-genders-berlin-300964","company_name":"Vexcash AG","title":"Software Developer .NET C# (all genders)","description":"

VEXCASH AG is Germany’s leading online provider of short-term loans. We offer our customers a quick and straightforward solution to bridge the gap until their next payday. More than 800,000 customers already rely on our service. Thanks to our innovative approach, they can secure financial liquidity without having to commit to a long-term agreement.

Aufgaben

We are looking for an experienced .NET/C# Developer to join our team and contribute to the development of modern web applications in the FinTech sector. You will work in a skilled and collaborative environment using modern Microsoft technologies (.NET 8+) to build reliable, maintainable, and high-quality software solutions. As a full-stack developer, you will contribute across the entire application stack, with a primary focus on backend services and APIs, while also supporting frontend development where needed.

Responsibilities:

  • Develop clean, maintainable, testable, and reusable C# code based on business requirements and user stories
  • Design, develop, and maintain applications using ASP.NET Core MVC, ASP.NET Core Razor Pages, and Entity Framework Core.
  • Design and implement RESTful APIs following best practices and scalable architecture principles
  • Contribute to frontend development using HTML5, CSS, Bootstrap, JavaScript, and TypeScript
  • Work with SQL Server, including data modelling, query optimization, and performance tuning
  • Implement automated tests (unit and integration) to ensure software quality
  • Collaborate using Git-based workflows and participate in code reviews
  • Contribute to CI/CD pipelines and automated deployments
  • Work with Microsoft Azure services and cloud-based architectures
  • Analyze, troubleshoot, and resolve technical and performance issues
  • Contribute to continuous improvement of code quality, architecture, and development processes

Qualifikation

  • Strong professional experience with C# and the .NET ecosystem
  • Hands-on experience with .NET Framework (maintenance and enhancement of legacy applications) and .NET 8+ / ASP.NET Core for modern application development
  • Solid experience with ADO.NET and Entity Framework Core
  • Experience designing and building RESTful APIs
  • Strong knowledge of SQL Server, relational database design, and query optimization.
  • Experience with frontend technologies (HTML5, JavaScript/TypeScript, CSS)
  • Experience with automated testing frameworks (e.g., xUnit, NUnit, MSTest)
  • Good understanding of software architecture principles and design patterns
  • Experience using Git in collaborative development environments
  • Familiarity with CI/CD pipelines and tooling
  • Experience with Microsoft Azure
  • Experience working in agile development environments
  • Strong problem-solving skills and focus on code quality
  • Good command of English and German

Benefits

  • We currently offer the Deutschlandticket on a 100% basis (available to employees only)
  • We currently offer membership of Urban Sports (available to employees only)
  • Fresh fruit baskets, hot and cold drinks in our office
  • An international, dynamic, committed and supportive team
  • An office located right next to Berlin’s main railway station Hauptbahnhof, designed in the style of a co-working space
  • Hybrid Working

About The Role

Taktile empowers financial institutions to transform into truly AI-native organizations. We’re growing rapidly with enterprise customers across banks and insurance companies, and we’re looking for a Strategic GTM Lead for Insurance in DACH: someone who has led client engagements at a top-tier strategy consultancy and now wants to build a market rather than advise on one. You will decide which insurers we go after and why, develop those relationships from first contact to signed partnership, and be the person senior insurance executives trust to think through how AI changes underwriting, claims and operations in their business.

This is not a classic sales role. You will open new strategic insurance accounts and grow them into long-term partnerships, from the first executive conversation to large, account-level commitments. Our Account Executives close individual deals and use cases; you set the direction for the account as a whole. Most of your impact comes from account strategy, executive dialogue, ecosystem work with consultancies and partners, and shaping how Taktile shows up in the German-speaking insurance market. You will work closely with our Head of Insurance, Account Executives, Solution Engineering, Product and Engineering.

What You'll Do

  • Identify and prioritize target accounts across DACH insurers (primary insurers, reinsurers, MGAs, insurance groups) based on a clear thesis: where the business case for AI-driven decisioning is strongest and where we can win

  • Build account strategies for your portfolio: map the organization, its strategic agenda and transformation programs, the buying committee and the path to an executive sponsor, and spot expansion opportunities from day one

  • Grow and retain accounts once they are live: steer the overall relationship, open new business lines and country organizations, and make sure clients see lasting value

  • Lead relationships at every level, from claims and underwriting heads to CIOs, COOs and board members, and move them from first conversation to a defined business case and a strategic commitment to Taktile

  • Design and moderate executive workshops and steering meetings with insurance leadership teams, turning open-ended ambitions ("we need to become AI-native") into concrete, prioritized use cases

  • Shape and land account-level commitments (business case, commercial framework, executive sign-off), working hand in hand with the Account Executives who close individual deals, Solution Engineering and our Head of Insurance

  • Work closely with Product and Engineering to tailor our platform to each client's needs and turn client requirements into concrete solutions

  • Build and work our ecosystem in DACH: strategy and technology consultancies, system integrators and core system vendors who shape insurers' technology decisions

  • Represent Taktile at industry conferences, roundtables and client events, and help design formats of our own that bring insurance executives together

  • Bring market insight back into Taktile: what insurers need, how competitors and incumbents position, and what that means for our product, messaging and pricing

  • Help build the playbook for Taktile's insurance business in DACH as we scale the team

About You

  • 6+ years of total work experience, including 4–6 years at McKinsey, BCG, Bain or a comparable strategy or operations consultancy, ideally leading client teams as Engagement Manager, Project Leader or equivalent

  • Project experience with insurance clients; you don't need to be an insurance specialist, and adjacent work in operations, technical advisory or digital/AI transformation counts

  • A commercial track record: ideally you have sold or expanded projects as an Engagement Manager. Software sales experience is not required

  • Outgoing and client-facing: you enjoy being in front of clients and leading the conversation, rather than working in the background

  • You are comfortable in front of C-level executives: you can structure a difficult discussion, moderate a room of senior stakeholders and hold your own when challenged

  • Strong problem-structuring and business case skills; you can quantify the value of a use case and explain it to a CFO

  • Technical understanding: you can discuss how our platform works with engineers and translate it for business leaders

  • You take ownership of outcomes, not just recommendations, and you are motivated by building revenue and long-term client relationships. High ownership, but a team player, not a lone wolf

  • Fluent in German and English, written and spoken

  • Based in Munich or Berlin (Frankfurt or London possible) and happy to travel frequently across Germany, Austria and Switzerland. This is not a remote role: you will regularly work on-site with clients, for example in workshops

Ideal Qualifications (but not required)

  • Experience beyond consulting, for example in an industry or in-house role

  • Existing network among senior decision-makers at DACH insurers, insurance consultancies or core system vendors

  • Experience in an enterprise software, insurtech or AI company, for example in a commercial, strategy or business development role

  • Hands-on familiarity with how insurers run claims, underwriting or pricing, and with the regulatory context (BaFin, Solvency II, EU AI Act)

  • Experience speaking at industry events or publishing on insurance and AI topics

What We Offer

  • Work with colleagues that lift you up, challenge you, celebrate you and help you grow. We come from many different backgrounds, but what we have in common is the desire to operate at the very top of our fields. If you are similarly capable, caring, and driven, you'll find yourself at home here.

  • Make an impact and meaningfully shape an early-stage company.

  • Experience a truly flat hierarchy and communicate directly with founding team members. Having an opinion and voicing your ideas is not only welcome but encouraged, especially when they challenge the status quo.

  • Learn from experienced mentors and achieve tremendous personal and professional growth. Get to know and leverage our network of leading tech investors and advisors around the globe.

  • Receive a top-of-market equity and cash compensation package, with a predominantly fixed salary and a performance-based bonus.

  • Get access to a self-development budget you can use to e.g. attend conferences, buy books or take classes.

  • Use the equipment of your choice including meaningful home office set-up.

Our Stance

  • We're eager to meet talented and driven candidates regardless of whether they tick all the boxes. We're looking for someone who will add to our culture, not just fit within it. We strongly encourage individuals from groups traditionally underestimated and underrepresented in tech to apply.

About Us

Taktile enables financial institutions to transform into AI-native organizations that are increasingly powered by autonomous agents. With our modular Agentic Decision Platform, customers combine AI agents, rules, relevant context, and human oversight to safely automate and optimize their decisions—approving more customers, reimbursing claims instantly, stopping fraud before it spreads, and financing every business worth funding. Founded in 2020, Taktile powers millions of decisions daily for institutions including Mercury, Monzo, Faire, and Pleo. With offices in New York, Berlin, London, São Paulo, and Iași, the company has raised $184M from Growth Equity at Goldman Sachs Alternatives, Index Ventures, Tiger Global, Balderton Capital, and Y Combinator. At Adclear, we're building the trust layer for how the world's most regulated companies bring products to market. Contexte :

ENSTA est un établissement d’enseignement supérieur et de recherche sous tutelle du ministère des Armées. ENSTA accompagne par sa recherche, son innovation et son offre de formation la transformation des grands secteurs stratégiques nationaux répondant ainsi aux enjeux de souveraineté nationale. Elle dispose de 3 unités de formation et de recherche (UFR) organisées autour de 9 laboratoires de recherche (UER) qui mènent une recherche appliquée en relation étroite avec l’industrie.

 

ENSTA est membre fondateur de l’Institut Polytechnique de Paris (IP Paris). Dans le cadre d’IP Paris, l’école participe aux activités des centres interdisciplinaires notamment du centre interdisciplinaire d'études pour la Défense et la Sécurité (CIEDS, soutenu par le ministère des armées et l’agence de l’innovation de défense (AID)). Sujet : “Experimental Geomechanics for Induced Seismicity and Control”

Le poste fait partie du projet ERC-CdG « Preventing human-induced seismicity to fight climate change » (INJECT), financé par le Conseil européen de la recherche (ERC). La recherche sera menée à l'ENSTA, Institut Polytechnique de Paris. Le poste offre l'opportunité de travailler sur un sujet de recherche stimulant et à fort impact. Les connaissances, l'innovation et les compétences développées dans le cadre de ce poste offriront d'excellentes perspectives d'évolution de carrière tant dans l'industrie que dans le monde universitaire.

Le changement climatique constitue une menace imminente pour notre civilisation. Les nouvelles technologies les plus en vue pour lutter contre le changement climatique font appel aux ressources énergétiques renouvelables et durables du sous-sol de la Terre et au stockage souterrain. Cependant, toutes ces technologies dépendent de l'injection de fluides dans la croûte terrestre, ce qui peut provoquer d'importants tremblements de terre. INJECT résoudra ce problème en s'appuyant sur une nouvelle méthode scientifique révolutionnaire qui empêchera la sismicité induite par l'homme et maximisera la production et le stockage d'énergie à partir de ressources naturelles renouvelables et durables.

La méthodologie interdisciplinaire d'INJECT repose sur un programme scientifique astucieux qui place la théorie du contrôle et les mathématiques au cœur de ce nouveau défi. Sur la base de développements théoriques de pointe, des contrôleurs et des observateurs robustes seront conçus pour ajuster de manière optimale les taux d'injection de fluides, prévenir les événements sismiques induits sur de vastes régions et optimiser la production et le stockage d'énergie. Les méthodes théoriques innovantes d'INJECT seront testées en profondeur à l'aide de modèles numériques de haute fidélité qui tiendront compte de la dynamique poro-élasto, du frottement de Coulomb, de la multiphysique et de la modélisation d'ordre réduit. Le plan expérimental s'appuiera sur des démonstrateurs et des essais hybrides laboratoire-ordinateur pour tester la théorie.     About Hexa

    Hexa (formerly eFounders) gives entrepreneurs the best chances to build outstanding companies.

    We are a pioneering, world-leading startup studio born in Europe that designs, builds and launches category-defining startups. We are today recognized as one of the best venture studios in the world, with a track record comparable to tier-1 VC funds.

    We have created 60+ companies (including 3 unicorns) with a combined valuation of over $5 billion, among them Aircall, Spendesk, Front, Swan and Yousign.

    Hexa is in full growth mode, with three early-stage activities: our Ventures programs Hexa Start and Hexa Sprint which help entrepreneurs go from zero to one, and a PE program, Hexa Scale, which takes majority stakes in existing startups and pushes them to new thresholds.

    The hardware vertical at Hexa: Frontier Tech

    Frontier Tech is Hexa’s studio focused on physical tech, led by Guerric de Crombrugghe.

    We build companies that move atoms: real machines, deployed in the field, often for defense, energy, space and critical infrastructure. A few examples of what is on the bench today include containerized atmospheric water generators, expendable turbojets, and ship-borne satellite ground stations.

    Our edge is velocity. We go from idea to working hardware with small teams and lean budgets, against legacy players with hundreds of engineers and decade-long programs. AI is now the biggest lever we have to widen that gap, today by speeding up how we build, and tomorrow by shaping what kind of companies we build.

    Why this role, why now

    AI for hardware is moving faster than any team can track. Our internal map now tracks close to 200 tools, from text-to-CAD, AI-native electronics and physics surrogates to manufacturing, test data, procurement and the MCP connectors that let agents drive CAD and EDA tools directly.

    Most of these tools will not matter. A handful will cut weeks off our programs. We need someone whose job is to find those, prove them on our real parts, and put them in the hands of our founders before our competitors do.

    The mission

    We’re looking for an industrial hardware engineer who is 100% AI-pilled, with a dual objective:

    • Adopt AI inside our startups. Make every Frontier Tech venture the fastest-moving hardware team in its category, using the best AI tools available today.

    • Build companies that grow with AI. Design products and business models that are both AI-enabled (they get better with every new generation of models) and AI-enablers (they feed AI with the data, compute, energy or infrastructure it needs), and run the companies themselves on AI from day one. The goal is a positive feedback loop: the more AI grows, the more our companies grow.

    Adoption is the immediate focus. The role splits into two:

    80%: deploy AI inside our ventures

    Hands-on, embedded in the teams, measured by weeks saved.

    • Map the bottlenecks. Sit with each venture and map its engineering workflow, from requirements to design, simulation, electronics, firmware, test, manufacturing and documentation. Find the steps that cost the most weeks.

    • Do the engineering. You are part of the team, not an advisor. You will run the CAD, set up the simulations, push the PCB, write the firmware agent, build the digital twin, produce the documentation, build the tools that automate technical pre-sales material that wins a contract. You ship parts and files, not slides.

    • Run the shared AI infrastructure. Set up and maintain the agents, repos and connectors between tools (CAD, EDA, simulation, data), with a common setup across ventures, so founders spend their time engineering rather than configuring.

    • Make it stick. Start with hands-on workshops on each team’s real problems, then train founders and engineers, write the playbooks, and track real adoption so tools are used every day rather than demoed once.

    20%: studio radar and partnerships

    • Keep the map alive. Track the AI-for-hardware landscape and what frontier labs ship, and maintain our living map of tools, maturity and pricing.

    • See beyond the hype. Our founders want evidence, not promises. Benchmark tools on our own parts and problems, not on vendor demos, and tell the studio plainly where the value is and where it is not.

    • Close partnerships. Negotiate studio-wide deals with key players (early access, design-partner status, credits, preferential pricing) so every Hexa hardware venture starts with better conditions than it could get alone.

    • Build the default stack. Turn what works into a reusable AI toolkit that every new Frontier Tech venture gets on day one.

    • Design AI-native companies. Work with founders from day one on where AI sits in the product, how the business model captures value as models improve, which data to capture and own, and which workflows run on agents so the team scales without headcount growing in step with revenue.

    Who we’re looking for

    • An industrial hardware engineer. 3 to 7 years designing, building and testing physical products in aerospace, defense, energy, automotive, industrial equipment or a hardware startup. You have taken parts from CAD to the shop floor and know tolerancing, DFM, test campaigns and suppliers.

    • 100% AI-pilled. You use AI agents every day, you have built your own automations, and you have already tried text-to-CAD, AI simulation or AI electronics tools on real work. You switch setups as soon as something better ships, and you have opinions on how a hardware company should be built when much of its engineering is done by agents.

    • A skeptical builder. You judge tools by measured time saved, not by launch videos. You are as happy killing a tool as adopting one.

    About EH Energy Engineering

    EH Energy is developing cutting-edge fuel cell technology for heavy-duty mobility and large-scale stationary power applications. Our uniquely redesigned product delivers a significantly more compact fuel cell system with high power density and lower production costs. In response to the challenges of climate change and the global shift toward decentralized energy, EH Energy provides high-performance, cost-effective fuel cell solutions to our clients and partners.

    To support our rapid growth and bring our systems to global markets, we are seeking a Certification Engineer. In this critical role, you will take full ownership of our product compliance roadmap, bridging the gap between innovative engineering and strict global regulations. You will lead hazard and risk assessments, define certification strategies across international markets (EU, North America, marine), and interface directly with notified bodies and classification societies to ensure our fuel cell systems are safe, fully compliant, and market-ready.

    This role requires a full-time, on-site presence at our office in Nyon, Switzerland. We are unable to offer remote or hybrid arrangements, so candidates should be based locally or prepared to relocate.

     

    Key responsibilities

    Certification strategy and project management

    • Identify applicable directives, regulations, harmonised standards and class rules early in the development cycle and translate them into design requirements (EU, North America, marine)

    • Select and manage notified bodies, NRTLs, classification societies and test laboratories, own budgets, schedules and contracts for certification work

    • Plan and witness type tests, factory acceptance tests (FAT) and site acceptance tests (SAT)

    Safety engineering and risk analysis

    • Lead risk assessments to ISO 12100 and hazard studies (HAZID, HAZOP to IEC 61882)

    • Lead design and process FMEA (IEC 60812) for stacks, balance of plant, containers and fuel processing

    • Run explosion-protection assessments: hazardous area classification (IEC 60079-10-1), ventilation and gas detection concepts, and equipment selection

    • Specify and verify safety functions to ISO 13849 (PL) and IEC 61508, including safety requirement specifications and validation reports

    Compliance and technical documentation

    • Compile and maintain technical construction files, CE Declarations of Conformity, type-approval dossiers and certification reports

    • Write and review user, installation, operation and maintenance manuals, safety instructions and labelling

    • Maintain the standards register and assess the impact of new or revised standards

    • Manage certification change control: assess design changes for impact on existing certificates

    Collaboration and continuous improvement

    • Act as the internal authority on certification scope: ensure in-service conformity of series production with certified designs, and support procurement and supply chain on material and packaging compliance (e.g. RoHS, packaging regulations).

    • Support design reviews and supplier qualification, including component certificates (ATEX, PED, electrical)

    Standards and regulatory scope

    The role covers, but is not limited to, the frameworks below. Working knowledge of most is expected; deep expertise in several is required

    • IEC 62282 series, CSA/ANSI FC 1:2021, ISO 16110-1 and Machinery Regulation (EU) 2023/1230

       

    Required qualifications

    • Master’s or bachelor’s degree in mechanical, electrical, chemical, process or safety engineering, or equivalent

    • 5+ years in product certification, compliance or safety engineering for complex electromechanical or process equipment (energy, gas, process, machinery or marine)

    • Direct experience with hydrogen or fuel cell systems and the IEC 62282 series, CSA/ANSI FC 1 or ISO 16110

    • Proven track record of taking products through CE marking and third-party certification with notified bodies or NRTLs

    • Hands-on experience leading FMEA, HAZOP and risk assessments, and documenting them to auditor standard

    • Solid knowledge of ATEX / IECEx, hazardous area classification and explosion-protection concepts

    • Experience specifying and validating safety functions to ISO 13849 and/or IEC 61508

    • Excellent technical writing: clear, structured, audit-ready technical files and manuals

    • Fluent English, written and spoken

       

    Preferred qualifications and personal profile

    Nice to have

    • Marine type approval with a classification society (DNV, LR, BV, ABS) or IGF Code projects

    • Experience with fuel processing, reformers or fire equipment, and with pressure equipment under PED

    • Certified functional safety qualification or ATEX/IECEx competence certification

    • Familiarity with North American codes (NEC, NFPA) and UL/CSA certification

    Personal profile

    • Rigorous and structured, with a strong safety mindset and an eye for detail

    • Pragmatic: finds compliant solutions that keep development moving

    • Confident communicator with engineers, auditors, authorities and customers

    • Self-driven in a fast-growing, scale-up environment; comfortable owning topics end to end

       

    Start date: Immediately

    Help organisaties om data en AI verantwoord, betrouwbaar en effectief in te zetten.

    Data- en AI-governance is meer dan beleid en procedures. Het zorgt ervoor dat organisaties grip krijgen op hun data, betere beslissingen nemen en AI op een verantwoorde manier kunnen inzetten.

    • Je analyseert en verbetert processen rondom datakwaliteit, metadata en data lineage.

    • Je houdt rekening met privacy, security, Responsible AI en relevante wet- en regelgeving, zoals de EU AI Act.

    • Je presenteert analyses, bevindingen en aanbevelingen op een duidelijke en overtuigende manier.

    • Je ondersteunt klanten bij het invoeren van nieuwe processen en werkwijzen en helpt draagvlak te creëren.

    • Je signaleert kansen voor aanvullende dienstverlening en bespreekt deze met je team.

    Role - Software Engineer - Optimisation Team

    Company - iwell - Harmonizing Clean Energy

    Location - Utrecht


    About iwell

    At iwell, we are all about reinforcing energy security. We help European businesses become more energy independent. With growing regulations, extreme price volatility and rising grid issues, they need to be resilient. It is time to take charge and think ahead.

    We deliver energy management solutions that ensure that businesses are always in control of their energy. Our in-house developed EMS and modular battery storage drive profit through sustainability, making businesses future-proof. 

    We are a fast-growing international team of bold, talented individuals. From engineers and software developers to creative thinkers and customer-focused business developers. No matter what your strong suit is, we always are looking for people who are determined to make a positive impact.


    The Role

    The Optimisation team builds the Python applications that decide what our customers' energy assets should do, and when. Batteries, EV fleets, solar and grid connections all come together in our optimiser, and the team turns prices, forecasts and constraints into schedules and decisions that run in production every day.

    Much of this work has an operations-research flavour, and the problems rarely arrive neatly defined.. They arrive as a customer who needs their vans charged by 6:00 at the lowest cost or a battery whose value depends on the hour. We're looking for someone who is comfortable across that whole path: understanding the real-world problem, shaping it into something a computer can solve, and shipping and operating the result. You don't need to be an OR specialist. You do need to be a strong Python engineer who enjoys messy, concrete problems.

    Success in this role means being able to:

    • Take a loosely defined operational problem and turn it into working, maintainable production code.

    • Work with data and models (optimisation, forecasting or plain statistics) without losing sight of the engineering.

    What you will do

    • Create charging schedules for EV fleets that minimise electricity costs while guaranteeing every vehicle is ready when it needs to be. This means modelling tariffs, grid limits and departure times, and handling what happens when reality deviates from the plan.

    • Calculate the value of each kWh produced or consumed, so that batteries, solar and flexible loads are steered by what energy is actually worth at that moment, and customers can see where their savings come from.

    • Build forecasting models that predict operational issues before they happen, to maximise asset uptime and reduce the number of support tickets our Operations team has to handle.

    • Take your work all the way to production: packaging, deployment, monitoring and bugfixing.

    • Work with the rest of the Optimisation team on the shared tooling, data pipelines and modelling conventions the team uses..


    What are looking for

    • 5+ years of production Python development experience, writing clean, tested, maintainable code.

    • A proven ability to translate real-world problems into working code.

    • A pragmatic mindset: you choose the boring, well-understood solution when it's the right one, and you know when it isn't.

    • Strong communication skills and a habit of documenting your work. Fluency in English is required.

    • Weekly working hours of 32-40 hours 

    • Coming into the office 3-4 days per week

Worum gehts?

Du baust lieber mit Open Source als mit Lizenzschlüsseln und automatisierst alles, was dir in die Finger kommt?

Dann bist du bei uns richtig! Wir suchen einen Platform Engineer, der Lust auf langfristige Kundenprojekte hat und Plattformen aus Open-Source-Bausteinen baut – von Linux und Automatisierung über CI/CD bis zu Containern, egal ob in der Public Cloud, im Rechenzentrum des Kunden oder irgendwo dazwischen. Kurz: einen Generalisten für den ganzen Stack, der auch mal eine gewachsene Anwendung kubernetifiziert.

Wir bei cloudpunks glauben daran, dass wir den Unterschied machen können! Wir konzipieren, implementieren und betreiben Plattform- und Cloud-Lösungen – als Kubernetes Certified Service Provider (KCSP) und CNCF Silver Member.

Du bist Teil unseres Teams und stehst im direkten Kontakt mit unseren Kunden & Partnern. In gemeinsamen Projekten modernisieren wir Anwendungen, bauen Plattformen aus Open-Source-Bausteinen und sorgen dafür, dass alles automatisiert ausgebracht und betrieben wird. Wir wollen geile Projekte umsetzen – mit cooler Technologie, die dem Kunden wirklich hilft!

Deine Aufgaben!

Das machst du bei uns:

  • Anwendungen kubernetifizieren: Du nimmst Bestandsanwendungen auseinander, schreibst Dockerfiles und Helm Charts und bringst sie sauber auf Kubernetes – von der Java-Monolithen-Altlast bis zum frischen Microservice.

  • Plattformen aus Open-Source-Bausteinen: Aufbau von Kubernetes-Plattformen mit dem, was das CNCF-Ökosystem hergibt: Ingress-Controller, cert-manager, Harbor als Registry, Keycloak für Identity, Vault oder OpenBao für Secrets. Cloud-agnostisch, On-Premises oder hybrid.

  • Infrastructure as Code: Terraform bzw. OpenTofu, Ansible, Helm und Kustomize – du automatisierst alles, was automatisiert werden kann, und gießt jede Komponente in versionierten Code.

  • CI/CD & GitOps: Aufbau und Optimierung von CI/CD-Pipelines mit GitLab CI oder GitHub Actions. GitOps-Workflows mit ArgoCD oder Flux.

  • Security & Policies: Policies mit Kyverno oder OPA/Gatekeeper, Image-Scanning mit Trivy, Runtime-Security mit Falco. Du baust sichere Baselines ab Tag 1.

  • Observability: Aufbau von Monitoring-Stacks mit Prometheus, Grafana, Loki und OpenTelemetry – du sorgst dafür, dass unsere Kunden wissen, was auf ihrer Plattform passiert. Mit OpenCost auch, was sie kostet.

  • Backup, Recovery & Lifecycle: Backup- und Restore-Konzepte mit Velero, Cluster- und Komponenten-Upgrades, Lifecycle-Management. Du sorgst dafür, dass die Plattform nicht nur läuft, sondern auch wiederherstellbar und wartbar bleibt – als Code, nicht per Klick.

  • Kundenberatung & Befähigung: Du arbeitest embedded in Kundenteams, nimmst an Standups teil und befähigst Teams, ihre Plattform selbstständig zu betreiben.

Projektbeispiele aus unserem Alltag:

  • Containerisierung gewachsener Java-Anwendungen und Umzug auf Kubernetes für ein Finanzunternehmen

  • On-Premises-Kubernetes-Plattform mit Harbor, Keycloak und ArgoCD für ein Industrieunternehmen

  • Migration von VM-basierten Workloads auf Kubernetes mit Helm und GitLab CI für ein E-Commerce-Unternehmen

  • Secrets-Management mit Vault und Policy-as-Code mit Kyverno für ein Versicherungsunternehmen

  • Observability-Stack mit Prometheus, Grafana, Loki und OpenTelemetry für ein Healthcare-Unternehmen

  • Backup- und Restore-Konzept mit Velero für ein Logistikunternehmen



Dein Profil

Must-have (ohne das wird's schwer):

  • Linux & Container: Solide Linux-Kenntnisse und Erfahrung mit Docker bzw. Containern – du weißt, was im Container passiert und warum.

  • Kubernetes: Mindestens 2 Jahre praktische Erfahrung mit Kubernetes, egal ob Vanilla, in der Cloud oder On-Premises.

  • Infrastructure as Code: Erfahrung mit Terraform/OpenTofu oder Ansible sowie Helm und/oder Kustomize.

  • CI/CD: Erfahrung mit mindestens einem CI/CD-Tool (GitLab CI, GitHub Actions, Jenkins) für automatisierte Deployments.

  • Networking: Verständnis von DNS, TLS, Load Balancing und Container-Networking.

Nice-to-have (macht dich noch interessanter):

  • GitOps: Erfahrung mit ArgoCD oder Flux.

  • Security: Erfahrung mit Kyverno, OPA/Gatekeeper, Trivy, Falco oder Vault.

  • Observability: Erfahrung mit Prometheus, Grafana, Loki oder OpenTelemetry.

  • Identity & Registry: Erfahrung mit Keycloak und Harbor.

  • Cloud-Provider: Erste Erfahrung mit AWS oder Azure schadet nicht – ist aber kein Muss.

  • Zertifizierungen: CKA, CKAD, CKS, LFCS oder andere CNCF-Zertifizierungen.

Was du mitbringen solltest:

  • Kommunikation: Du kannst technische Konzepte verständlich erklären – auf Deutsch und Englisch.

  • Eigenverantwortung: Du arbeitest selbstständig und übernimmst Verantwortung für deine Arbeit.

  • Teamfähigkeit: Du arbeitest gerne embedded in Kundenteams und bist ein Teamplayer.

  • Lernbereitschaft: Du bleibst am Ball und lernst kontinuierlich neue Technologien.

About Grubel

Grubel is a research lab that builds AI for high-stakes knowledge work, starting with law. Legal matters require specialized expertise, and each one involves its own facts, practices, parties, and institutions. General-purpose AI applies the same system to every legal matter, varying only what goes into a limited context window.

To meet the depth and diversity of legal work, we let every matter build its own AI: engineer the right data for the matter, adapt the model and agent to it, and track what improves. We combine the three into a matter-specific improvement loop that runs until the system delivers what the matter demands.

The lab has offices in Munich and Tübingen.

Schlank, schnell, transparent – und nach Profil gestaffelt. Das gemeinsame Mittagessen ist der tägliche Ankerpunkt – wer im Büro ist, isst mit; erwartet, nicht kontrolliert. Das Abendessen ist dasselbe Angebot ohne jede Erwartung. Beides ohne Eigenanteil. About TACTILIA

At TACTILIA, we are building the industry-ready robotic hand that closes one of the biggest gaps in Physical AI. Spun out of SCHUNK, the global market leader in gripping technology, we combine a decade of robotic-hand expertise and real industrial access with the speed and ambition of a deep-tech startup.

This isn't a research project waiting for its first customer. We already have a product, customers are ready to use it, and we are launching now. Your work will directly shape the electronics, actuators, and embedded systems that make that possible.

You will join at the moment when the hard engineering questions become real product decisions: how do we make a highly capable robotic hand reliable, manufacturable, serviceable, and simple enough to deploy on a real shop floor?

The Role

As Senior Industrialization & Supply Chain Manager you will take ownership of the industrialization perspective throughout the product development process. Working closely with R&D, engineering and external manufacturing partners, you will ensure that manufacturing considerations are integrated into product design from the earliest development stages.

You will challenge existing design decisions where necessary, identify more suitable manufacturing technologies and processes, and drive the transition from engineering concepts and prototypes to manufacturable, scalable products.

This is a key role for someone who enjoys operating at the intersection of engineering, product development and manufacturing – and who is equally comfortable discussing technical trade-offs with R&D engineers, negotiating with suppliers and engaging directly with people on the production floor.

What you will do:

  • Drive industrialization from early product development: Work closely with R&D engineers from the beginning of the development process, integrating manufacturing expertise into design decisions and challenging concepts where necessary to improve manufacturability, cost and scalability.

  • Define manufacturing strategies and technologies: Evaluate, select and implement appropriate manufacturing technologies, processes and production methods for complex mechanical and electromechanical components.

  • Optimize product design for manufacturing: Identify opportunities to simplify designs, reduce component complexity, improve production feasibility and find more cost-effective manufacturing solutions without compromising product performance.

  • Drive design for manufacturing of electronics and sensorics hardware: Work with R&D on the hardware design of electronics and sensor systems (PCBs, sensor modules, cabling and assembly) with manufacturing and supply chain requirements in mind. Ensure designs are producible, testable, cost-efficient and robust in series production.

  • Develop external manufacturing partnerships: Identify and establish relationships with suitable manufacturing partners, particularly specialised SMEs. Work directly with company owners, technical experts and production teams to identify solutions and build reliable partnerships.

  • Build up the supply chain and procurement strategy: Define and implement the supply chain and procurement strategy together with SCHUNK SE and external partners. Leverage SCHUNK's established supplier network and purchasing expertise where it makes sense, and build additional sourcing channels, including second sources, for critical components.

  • Drive manufacturing readiness: Take ownership of manufacturing bottlenecks, technical feasibility, supplier lead times and production challenges, ensuring a smooth transition from prototypes to repeatable and scalable production.

  • Build industrialization capabilities: Establish manufacturing processes, methods and standards that support TACTILIA's future growth and increasing production requirements.

What you bring:

  • Several years (5 years) of experience in industrialization, manufacturing engineering, production engineering or a comparable technical role.

  • Broad knowledge of manufacturing technologies and processes, ideally involving complex mechanical, precision or electromechanical products.

  • Proven experience translating engineering designs into practical, cost-efficient and manufacturable products.

  • Experience with design for manufacturing of electronics and sensor hardware (PCB assembly, component selection, test strategies), ideally in an electromechanical or mechatronic product.

  • Experience identifying, evaluating and working with external manufacturing partners and suppliers.

  • Experience building or managing supply chains and procurement strategies, including working with a parent or group company's purchasing organization.

  • Comfortable engaging with different stakeholders, from R&D engineers and senior management to supplier owners, technicians and blue-collar production teams.

  • Entrepreneurial, pragmatic and hands-on mindset, with the ability to take ownership and drive topics independently.

  • Strong communication skills and the confidence to challenge engineering decisions constructively.

  • Fluent in English; German is an advantage.

The next chapter of robotics won't be built in a lab. It will be built by people who care about what happens when technology meets the real world.

At TACTILIA, you'll work on one of the hardest open problems in robotics: giving machines the dexterity, reliability and robustness to interact with the physical world at industrial scale.

The technology is taking shape, the team is being built, and the standards around robotic hands and their skills are still open. That means your decisions will have a lasting impact — not just on a product, but on what comes next for Physical AI.

Build the hand. Define the standard. Shape what comes next.

If you're excited by the challenge of building robotic hands that work reliably in the real world, we'd love to hear from you.

  • Own your destiny: Operate as a pure revenue leader, responsible for 80-90% net-new logo acquisition through self-sourced pipeline.

Engineering Manager

Location: Remote - Europe (CET ±2 hours)

About FullEnrich:

Every go-to-market motion runs on data, but no single provider has ever had complete coverage. We solve that problem: instead of relying on a single data source, we orchestrate 20+ premium providers around the world, automatically querying them and verifying data in real-time until we find the best available contact information. The result is industry-leading coverage and data quality, helping sales and GTM teams connect with the right people faster.

What started as a better way to find emails and phone numbers has grown into a broader vision: becoming the trusted GTM data infrastructure layer powering modern revenue teams and AI agents. Today, more than 6,000 customers, including companies like AWS, Deel, HubSpot, Clay, Intercom, Unify,and Artisan, trust us to power their prospecting and enrichment.

Founded in Paris and now headquartered in San Francisco, we're a team of 50+ people across the US, Europe, LATAM, and Israel, growing quickly and building with speed, ownership, and ambition. That's where you come in.

The Role:

You'll be joining as an Engineering Manager, reporting directly to our VP of Engineering.

As FullEnrich continues to grow, we're investing in the engineering leadership and structure needed to support our next stage of growth. We're looking for someone who combines strong people leadership with technical depth, and who enjoys building high-performing teams, improving how engineers work, and creating the foundations for sustainable growth.

You'll initially lead a multidisciplinary team of up to ten engineers across backend, frontend, and data, taking ownership of their development, performance, and delivery. Working closely with Product Managers and engineering leadership, you'll help translate business priorities into achievable engineering objectives, ensuring teams have the clarity, support, and processes they need to deliver great work.

This is an opportunity to have a real impact on how our engineering organization evolves. As we scale toward 25 engineers, you'll help shape our squad structure, establish effective ways of working, and build an environment where engineers can grow and do their best work. You'll work closely with the VP of Engineering, CTO, and other Engineering Managers, with the autonomy to influence decisions and drive meaningful improvements across the organization.

What You'll Do:

People Leadership & Development

  • Lead, coach, and develop engineers through regular 1:1s, performance management, feedback, and career development.

  • Build a supportive, high-performing team environment where engineers have clear expectations, opportunities to grow, and the autonomy to do their best work.

  • Take ownership of team health, engagement, and retention, proactively identifying and addressing challenges.

Hiring & Team Growth

  • Own the engineering side of hiring for your squads, including defining requirements, setting assessment criteria, interviewing, and making hiring decisions.

  • Develop effective onboarding processes that help new engineers become productive and autonomous quickly.

  • Partner with engineering leadership to shape team structure, squad ownership, and hiring priorities as the organization scales.

Engineering Delivery & Execution

  • Partner with Product Managers to translate product and business priorities into clear engineering objectives, realistic roadmaps, and measurable outcomes.

  • Own engineering delivery across your squads, ensuring work is appropriately scoped, estimated, and delivered with clear accountability.

  • Identify and manage delivery risks, technical dependencies, and competing priorities, keeping stakeholders informed and addressing blockers early.

Engineering Processes & Continuous Improvement

  • Own and continuously improve how your squads operate, using our Discovery → Run lifecycle, inspired by Shape Up, and DORA metrics to measure delivery effectiveness.

  • Establish practical, scalable ways of working that improve predictability, collaboration, and engineering quality without introducing unnecessary bureaucracy.

  • Collaborate with other Engineering Managers and the VP of Engineering to evaluate and improve engineering processes across the wider organization.

Technical Leadership & Cross-Functional Collaboration

  • Provide technical guidance on architectural decisions, engineering trade-offs, and complex delivery challenges, ensuring teams make well-informed decisions.

  • Work closely with Product, Design, Support, Sales, and leadership to align engineering priorities with business needs.

  • Communicate progress, risks, and trade-offs clearly, creating transparency and trust across teams and stakeholders.

Our Tech Stack

Our backend is built in Go (Golang), with Svelte on the frontend, PostgreSQL and OpenSearch for data, and DigitalOcean for cloud infrastructure. We use Docker, GitHub Actions, and Grafana to support deployment, automation, and observability, with a modular hexagonal monolith architecture.

You won't need to be hands-on with every technology, but you'll bring the technical understanding to challenge architectural decisions, navigate trade-offs, and support your engineers in solving complex problems.

What Success Looks Like:

By 3 months

  • You've built a strong understanding of our product, technology, engineering processes, and business objectives, establishing trusted relationships with your engineers and key stakeholders.

  • You've taken ownership of people management across your squads, with regular 1:1s, clear expectations, and an understanding of each engineer's strengths and development needs.

  • You've assessed current delivery practices, team structure, and performance, identifying opportunities to improve collaboration, predictability, and team effectiveness.

By 6 months

  • Your squads are operating with clear objectives, defined ownership, and measurable KPIs aligned with product and business priorities.

  • You've established effective delivery practices, with more predictable planning, proactive risk management, and improved visibility for stakeholders.

  • You've identified team capability gaps and are actively contributing to hiring, onboarding, and the development of engineers across your squads.

  • You're contributing meaningful improvements to engineering processes and organizational structure alongside the wider engineering management team.

By 12 months

  • Your squads consistently deliver against realistic, well-defined roadmaps, with clear accountability, effective collaboration, and measurable improvements in delivery performance.

  • Engineers have clear development paths, receive regular feedback, and feel supported in their growth, contributing to strong engagement and retention.

  • New engineers are onboarding efficiently and becoming productive quickly, supported by established processes and a clear engineering hiring bar.

  • You've helped shape a scalable engineering organization with well-defined squad ownership, effective ways of working, and stronger alignment between Engineering, Product, and the wider business.

  • Stakeholders have confidence in engineering delivery, with transparent communication, reliable planning, and fewer unexpected blockers.
